# Offense and Defense Deep Dive Analysis

Report 080 | Published 2022-03-20 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2022-3-20/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/080.json)

Selective offense accompanies explicit macro uncertainty.

The article acknowledges uncertainty more clearly than a simple bullish/bearish label would suggest. Its preferred China bottom failed and the legislative reassurance missed the IRA. DHI remained operationally resilient while earnings fell. The bank-asset heuristic deserves particular scrutiny after SVB: low credit risk did not eliminate duration or funding risk.

**Coverage:** All article text blocks were read. Ledger covers material macro, investment, and causal propositions; incidental descriptive statistics, boilerplate, and unreasoned position lists are excluded. Image labels were read, not image pixels.

## Claims

### 080-C01

**China relaxes economic restrictions**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | 2022 |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | cautious expectation |
| Asset or variable | china-2022-reopening-optimism |
| Source blocks | 11, 27, 188 |
| Thesis family | china-2022-reopening-optimism |

The described Shenzhen reopening and market-support signals were real localized changes, while the stronger nationwide turning-point interpretation proved premature as lockdowns continued. China eventually reopened late 2022, so a blanket wrong verdict on all relaxation would ignore part of the observed path.

**Direction:** Partial support; distinguish observed indicators from inferred aggregate outcome.

**Timing:** Assessed against the stated horizon: 2022

**Mechanism:** A matching outcome alone does not establish causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Final verification of 2022 GDP](https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202401/t20240110_1946428.html) | National Bureau of Statistics of China | 2023-12-29 | Verified in the audit

2022 growth was 3.0%; real estate contracted.

- [China growth normalization disrupted](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/06/08/covid-19-outbreaks-and-headwinds-have-disrupted-china-s-growth-normalization-world-bank-report) | World Bank | 2022-06-08 | Verified in the audit

After a strong early-2022 start, Omicron outbreaks and mobility restrictions disrupted growth normalization.

## Framework lessons

- Separate business resilience from share-price volatility.
- Retain cash when indicators conflict.

## Verification limitations

- Captured website text is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- Chart-only numerical claims have not been visually verified.
- Selected stock/ETF adjusted-close comparisons are disclosed where used; no reconstructed portfolio backtest has been performed.
- Unresolved verdicts are not forecast failures or successes; no aggregate hit rate is inferred.
